title: Asking the pope (1887)
hook: everyone in line is told to stay silent; a girl from France has a request, and her sister whispers: speak
tomorrow: the pope said 'if God wills.' so did the door open?

segments.voice: A week of Thérèse growing up: a sister who left, a statue's smile, a kiss of love, a long fear, a staircase, a condemned man. Yesterday's line: my first child.

There's always a rule about who gets to talk. Wait to be called on. Players don't argue with the ref. No questions at the end. A long line of pilgrims moves past an old man in white, and everyone has been told the same thing: kneel, receive his blessing, and say nothing. A girl in the line has a request she has carried all the way from France. Her sister leans in and whispers one word: speak.
screen: `A RULE ABOUT WHO TALKS.` → `KNEEL, AND SAY NOTHING.` → `HER SISTER WHISPERS: SPEAK.`

segments.voice: First, the closed doors. Thérèse wanted to enter Carmel young. The priest in charge of the convent said wait, and the bishop hadn't said yes. So she went to Rome on pilgrimage with her father and Céline. Second, the request. Kneeling before Pope Leo the Thirteenth, despite the order to keep silent, she asked: Most Holy Father, in honor of your jubilee, let me enter Carmel at fifteen. Third, the answer. The vicar general nearby said the superiors were already looking into it. The pope told her, kindly, to do what the superiors said. She pressed. He looked at her and said she would enter if God willed it. Then the guards led her away, in tears. Fourth, the ball. She had offered herself to the child Jesus as his little ball, a toy he could play with, leave in a corner, or prick to see inside. In Rome, she says, he pricked his little ball, let it fall, and went to sleep. She asked boldly, and left the answer with God.
screen: `THE DOORS WERE CLOSED.` · `SHE KNELT AND ASKED.` · `IF GOD WILLS IT.` · `THE LITTLE BALL, PRICKED.` · then, large: `SHE ASKED THE POPE.`

segments.voice: Walk slowly for a minute, around a room or down a hall, carrying one good thing you've been afraid to ask for, the way she carried hers down that line. When you stop, say it once, plainly, out loud. If you pray, you can bring it with Jesus's words in Matthew: Ask, and it shall be given you.
Asking the pope. Thérèse's bold request to Leo the Thirteenth, against the rule to keep silent.
The line to keep: she asked the pope, boldly, with an open hand for the answer. Bye for now.
